turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Would you mind starting with telling me what I can help you with today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, um I haven't been feeling very well over the past two days. I have had this cough, I'm feeling very short of breath and I'm feeling very feverish as well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, uh, have you checked your temperature?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't actually checked it, but I'm just feeling hot and I'm having chills.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, were you having like night sweats as well?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, yeah, last night I did get sweaty.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and when uh, when did you start feeling feverish?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Feverish, maybe around the same time like right after the cough and shortness of breath started, maybe like a day and a half ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. It's um, so the cough started about a day and a half ago as well?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Uh, did you have a cough prior to this or is it new?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's new.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, is it a dry cough? Or are you bringing up sputum or phlegm?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, it's uh yeah, it's um, it's dry most of the time, but once in a while I'll see some like yellow phlegm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, have you noticed any blood?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: All right, and have you had any chest pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No chest, well actually, when I try to take a really deep breath in, it, it hurts, my chest hurts.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, where do you feel the pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, it seems to be central on my chest.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Do you feel it radiating anywhere, like to your back or to either side?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, how would you describe the pain? Like sharp, dull?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, it's pretty sharp when I take a deep breath in.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How long does the pain last for, and is there anything that you do that makes it go away?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It was like less than a minute um, and, and it goes away when I like, if I try not to take a deep breath in.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, so it sounds like that it, the, the breathing is a trigger there, when you're breathing in deeply.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright. And have you had any wheeze?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, a little bit, yes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and uh, is the wheeze new as well?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um yes, that also started after the coughing and the shortness of breath.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright. And have you had any episodes of feeling like your heart's racing, or is it speeding really fast?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and you said it, yeah, you've been short of breath as well. Um, are you really short of breath now, and what sorts of things have been really bringing it on for you?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um it's, yeah, I'm still a little bit short of breath and I, I guess the shortness of breath gets worse when I'm walking or doing something physical.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay and did, is this new or did you have this before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's new.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, have you noticed any swelling in your in your legs or extremities?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And do you get short of breath if you lie down flat?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, not that I've noticed.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how many pillows do you sleep with?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, just the one.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay um, and have you had any headaches?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how about any eye redness or discharge?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you had a runny nose or felt congested?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, yeah a little bit. Yeah, I've been, yeah, I've been feeling a little congested.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And when did that start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, that started a little bit before the cough, actually.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and you're still feeling that now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Have you had a sore throat?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No sore throat.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and um, have you had any um, muscle aches or body pains?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I, yeah, I guess my muscle aches a little bit um, it's very dull though, it's not sharp.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and uh, how has your energy been? Have you been fatigued?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, my energy's been pretty low. Um, I've been feeling very tired.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and how long has that been going on for?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, for about the same amount of time. Like three days, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and have you had any abdominal pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about nausea or vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And any changes to your urinary habits, like pain or?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and um, how has your appetite been?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, it hasn't been the greatest because I haven't been feeling well, but I've still been eating.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, have you had any weight loss over the last several months?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no, not that I've noticed.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And uh, how about any changes to your sense of smell or sense of taste?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Sense of smell or taste, no, no changes there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um and then any skin changes or rashes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, um, so you've been experiencing this cough, uh, started a couple of days ago with um, shortness of breath, and you're bringing up sputum sometimes and, and a fever that's started a bit more recently, as well as having some night sweats.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you experienced any other symptoms?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no. Other than that, no symptoms.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see, and have you tried anything to make, make the symptoms better?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I've tried some Tylenol, I've tried some, um like, cough suppressants, but nothing seems to be helping.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, and have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no, not um, well actually, I have, I had, I have osteoporosis, for which I'm taking calcium and vitamin D, as well as like um, alendronate, alendronate, some sort of bisphosphonate.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, have you had any, uh, like bone fractures?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I had um, a hip fracture, like uh, two years ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay and um, and how is the recovery and mobility been?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, pretty good now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Oh, that's great. And uh, do you have any other medical conditions besides osteoporosis?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that I know.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And have you had any surgeries prior, um, aside from the hip surgery two years ago?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I had my wisdom teeth taken out, I've had my gallbladder taken out, um, and I, I had like um, I had a PE um, a long time ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and what happened around that time, with the pulmonary embolism? Did you, was there a trigger, like a surgery around that time? Or were you immobilized or anything?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, they think it happened right after my um, gallbladder removal 'cause I was in the hospital for a while.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and so were you on any medication for a period of time after that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, yeah, I was, but not anymore.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, okay. And um, are you taking any other medications besides the ones for your bones?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no, no other medications.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And do you have any allergies?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, uh, and then could you tell me a little bit about your living situation right now? Are you living with anybody and uh, whereabouts?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I live in an apartment by myself and um, it's in London.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, great, and do you have any supports in the home that, that help you with uh, any activities of daily living, like um, either dressing or bathing or making food or even doing some of the shopping?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So I am pretty independent for most things. Um, there will be like a CCAC care worker who comes in, uh, once in a while just to help me clean the house.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, so once in a while, is this like once a week or once, yeah, how often?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, once every two weeks.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, well that's great. It sounds like you're managing really well on your own. Um, do you have any other supports nearby, like family or, or friends?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I have some family close by um, my son lives close by, uh, and my daughter lives about 2 hours away. I'll see them about once a month.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Um, and do you smoke cigarettes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, yeah, I used to smoke, but I stopped about five years back.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Oh, congratulations on quitting.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So you quit five years ago, and how long did you smoke for and how much did you smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I used to smoke, not a lot, just like one or two a day, uh, and I did that for about 25 years.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and uh, do you drink alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I'll have like a glass of wine once in a while.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how often is once in a while? Is this, or how many drinks per week would you say?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, per week, maybe like three.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, and any uh, heart or lung conditions that run in the family?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, yeah so, there is um, like lung cancer, there's asthma, there's uh, COPD. All of that, someone, like my, both sides of my family had.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and uh, anybody in the family have like a bleeding disorder?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: A bleeding disorder, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, anybody else in the family have either a deep vein thrombosis or, or PE?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, um, and have you been around any, anybody who's been sick?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not recently.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and have you traveled anywhere outside of the city, or?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, so that was everything I wanted to ask about today. Was there anything that uh, that you wanted to add?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, those are all questions that I had. Um, do you think um, I need to be hospitalized, um, because I'm very short of breath, or do you think I can just um, stay at home? Do you think I need antibiotics?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, so we'll, we'll check your temperature and, and confirm the fever and um, check your oxygen levels as well. You might need oxygen, um, you're mentioning, with your shortness of breath. Um, and we will get a chest x-ray, and if um, we're seeing consolidation there, suggestive of pneumonia, you may need antibiotics that will cover, cover those, those bugs. However, your symptoms do overlap with COVID as well, and so it will be important to get a, um, COVID swab. But to answer if you will need a hospital stay, I think we'll need to at least wait until some of the investigations come back and, um, that will help determine how severe the symptoms are and we'll observe you over the next few hours, and if you are getting any worse or um, anything like that, then it might be a good idea, um, to uh, to be admitted.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay. Okay yeah, that sounds good. Thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: You're welcome.
